analysts.summary: Stockanalysis.com: 25 analysts rate it Hold on balance (5 Strong Buy, 4 Buy, 12 Hold, 2 Sell, 2 Strong Sell), with an average target of $20.35 (+23%). Recent actions: Scotiabank initiated at Buy with a $25 target (2 Sep) and Loop Capital initiated at Hold with $22 (8 Sep). Public.com's 17-analyst set averages $22.18. The FY26 consensus is revenue of $4.88B and EPS of $0.59.

bear: The Muddy Waters accounting allegations are still unresolved, and the heavy use of fair-value loan accounting keeps skepticism high.
Shares outstanding grew 14.5% YoY with no buyback, diluting per-share growth.
Rate hikes (now management's base case) and consumer credit risk in a personal-loan-heavy book.
Momentum is weak: the stock is near its 52-week low, institutions were net sellers in Q2, short interest is ~14.6%, and dealer gamma is negative near spot.
The tech platform segment is shrinking (accounts −16% YoY).
bull: Growth is still 30%+ with rising profitability: FY26 adj. EPS ~$0.60 vs $0.37 in 2025, and adj. EBITDA margin at 30%+.
Deposit funding ($45.5B, +$5.3B QoQ) and an 18.7% CET1 ratio give room to keep lending.
The CEO keeps buying in the open market ($2.25M in 2026), and TBV/share is up 56% YoY.
Options IV is near a 52-week low, so upside through earnings is cheap to express. The analyst average target is ~23% above the price.

competition.summary: SoFi competes with fintech lenders (LendingClub, Upstart), digital banks (Nu), brokerages (Robinhood) and big banks. Its edge is the bank charter's deposit funding and a multi-product ecosystem (1.54 products per member). The tech platform business (Galileo/Technisys) is shrinking. We could not find a reliable current market-share figure for personal loans in the sources read.

name: SoFi Technologies, Inc.

options.gexNote: Net GEX across both expiries (strikes $14–19) is about −$2.1M per 1% move. Dealers are short gamma at spot, which tends to amplify moves. The largest negative gamma sits at the $16 and $16.5 strikes (≈12.4k and 12.7k Oct 2 puts). The largest positive gamma sits at $17.5 (≈8.5k Oct 2 + ≈18.0k Oct 9 calls). Above ~$17.17 the gamma turns positive and should dampen moves. Open interest is from IBKR as of the 25 Sep close; the snapshot status was FROZEN.
options.ivNote: Underlying IV is 45.1% against 30-day HV of 46.7%. The 52-week IV percentile is only 5.6% (13-week: 20.3%), so options are cheap relative to their own history ahead of Q3 earnings.
options.strategy: This is information only; no orders. Because IV is historically cheap and gamma is negative, defined-risk long-premium structures are favoured over selling premium. Examples: a bullish Nov call spread (e.g. 17.5/20) spanning the ~Oct 27 earnings, or a put spread under the $16 put wall as a hedge for existing shares. Selling puts near $16 is less attractive while dealers are short gamma there.

politicians.summary: We found no US Congress member trades in SOFI in the last 12 months (Quiver Quantitative). The most recent were two small purchases by Rep. James Comer in January 2025.

financial.note: CET1 18.7%, Tier 1 leverage 16.5%, $45.5B deposits, TBV/share $7.34 (+56% YoY). Profitable, but FCF is structurally negative (−$8.8B TTM) because it originates loans.

flows.note: Short interest ~14.6% of shares. Institutions net sold ~95.7M shares in Q2 (763 buyers vs 342 sellers). The CEO has made repeated open-market buys. Dealer gamma is negative near spot.

growth.note: Adj. revenue +40% YoY, originations +69% to a record $14.8B, members +35%, products +42%. FY26 guide calls for 32–35% revenue growth.

moat.note: Bank charter gives low-cost deposit funding (NIM 5.98%). Cross-buy is at 51% and brand awareness at 10.4%. Personal loans are competitive, and the tech platform segment is shrinking (accounts −16% YoY).

momentum.note: −36.7% YTD and ~−42% over 1y. The price is near its 52w low of $14.88 (52w high $32.73) and has traded $15–19 since March.

valuation.note: 34.9x trailing / 22.7x forward P/E and ~2.3x P/TBV. That is a premium to lender peers (LC, UPST, NU) but cheap next to HOOD. The price sits inside the fair-value range.

summary: SoFi is executing well: Q2 2026 adjusted revenue rose 40% to $1.21B, net income rose 61% to $157M, members hit 15.8M, and FY26 guidance calls for ~$0.60 adjusted EPS. The stock is still down about 37% YTD (IBKR) after the March Muddy Waters short report, a stretched starting valuation, 14.5% YoY share dilution and fears of higher rates. At $16.58 it trades near 2.3x tangible book and ~23x forward earnings, inside our $14.50–$20.50 fair-value range, so it looks fairly valued with modest upside. Growth and capital are strong, but momentum, flows and a negative-gamma options setup argue for a Neutral stance into the ~Oct 27 Q3 print.

valuation.method: We triangulated three approaches. (a) Peer multiples: 18–25x forward EPS of ~$0.73 (implied by a 22.7x forward P/E) gives $13.1–18.3, and 2.0–2.5x TBV/share of $7.34 gives $14.7–18.4. (b) Earnings power: start from FY26 adj. EPS of $0.60, grow it 35%/yr to ~$1.09 in 2028, apply an 18x exit multiple ($19.7) and discount 2 years at 12% to get ~$15.7. (c) Analyst targets: $12 low, $20.35 average, $30 high. Blended fair value: $14.50 / $17.50 / $20.50.
valuation.note: EV/Sales for SOFI, NU, UPST and HOOD uses P/S or EV/revenue as reported by stockanalysis.com. Lender multiples are not strictly comparable. Peer growth rates were not in the pages read. SOFI's premium to LC and UPST reflects faster growth and bank-charter funding; its discount to HOOD reflects a lower-margin balance-sheet model.
